summary: The sample size and the phase and sponsor rankings compare derives from its fetched trials must be assembled in a function that takes those trials and performs no I/O, so the aggregation can be exercised without a live client.
reason: The assembly sat inside buildDrugProfile between a ctgovFetch and its return, reachable only behind a network call. The generated compare_test.go answered that by rebuilding the loop in its own test body, and the copy then drifted: production calls tallyPhases while the copy still tallies with an inline range over t.Phases, so the coverage never reaches the phaseless-trial guard. A reprint must not re-inline this assembly. The phase cap of 8 is deliberately fixed while sponsors honour --top-sponsors: phaseLabel maps the registry onto six buckets and passes unrecognised values through, so eight leaves room for two unmapped values, whereas a sample can hold hundreds of sponsors. Guarded by TestSummarizeTrialsReachesTallyPhases.
validated_outcome: Restoring the inline phase loop in place of the tallyPhases call fails TestSummarizeTrialsReachesTallyPhases (N/A bucket 0, want 2) and TestSummarizeTrialsDistributionCountsEntries (5 entries, want 7), while the generated TestCompareAggregation stays green.
